messages:
support-bot: ALERT: ticket #2345 — multiple customers reporting high tail latency for /v1/generate on model redwood-tt-7b. p99 ~ 1.2s, p50 ~ 80ms. Sample logs: 

  [2026-03-15T10:11:58Z] req_id=abc123 model=redwood-tt-7b tokens=18 duration=1240ms status=200
  [2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] req_id=abc126 model=redwood-tt-7b tokens=14 duration=1189ms status=200

please triage. /link to ticket #2345

maya (oncall): On it. I can reproduce a p99 spike in prod metrics around 10:12 UTC. No full deploys in the last hour per deploy-bot, but I'll check config rollouts.

maya (oncall): @deploy-bot any recent config rollouts to continuous_batcher?

deploy-bot: config-rollout redwood/continuous_batcher default-profile updated by liam at 2026-03-15T09:55:12Z (rollout id r-9834). Changes: `max_delay_ms` 20 -> 100, `max_batch_tokens` 4096 -> 8192.

deploy-bot: rollout status: ~95% applied across serving-nodes (partial).

liam (runtime): That 20->100 change was intended to improve throughput for large prompts. It will increase batching latency for short inputs. Did we gate by route?

anika (support): Customer repro steps: send synchronous small prompts (~10 tokens) at low qps from single client. Most requests are fast (~60ms) but some are ~1.1s. Attached curl snippet they used: 

  ```bash
  for i in {1..100}; do \\curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-tt-7b","input":"hi"}' & done
  ```

anika (support): They said this started after an A/B config change earlier today.

maya (oncall): That matches. Continuous batcher tradeoff: larger `max_delay_ms` increases average throughput but makes tail latency worse for small, latency-sensitive requests. Our traffic mix for redwood-tt-7b is ~70% short prompts — bad fit.

liam (runtime): Quick mitigation options:
- revert the `max_delay_ms` to 20 (fast)
- set per-model override: `redwood-tt-7b.max_delay_ms=25`
- enable route-priority so latency-sensitive keys bypass batching
- add early-flush for small token counts (short-term hack)

maya (oncall): I'll roll back the rollout for redwood/continuous_batcher default-profile and apply a per-model override. Rolling now.

maya (oncall): PATCH call I'm using: 

  ```http
  PATCH /api/v1/configs/continuous_batcher/r-9834
  Content-Type: application/json
  {"targets": ["models:redwood-tt-7b"], "overrides": {"max_delay_ms": 25}}
  ```

maya (oncall): Applied override to redwood-tt-7b, and reverted default-profile to `max_delay_ms=20`. Watching metrics.

ops-bot: config-change r-9834 override applied to 12/12 serving-nodes for target redwood-tt-7b.

maya (oncall): After override, p99 dropped from ~1200ms -> ~220ms within 60s. p95 back near previous baseline. Confirming with synthetic repro from anika.

anika (support): Re-ran customer curl test against prod: distribution looks much better: majority <200ms, tail reduced. Customer notified. They want root cause explanation and ETA for permanent fix.

liam (runtime): Root cause summary for them: the A/B config increased batching delay globally which is great for throughput with long prompts but caused increased tail for routes dominated by short prompts. We should:
1) Add per-route defaults in rollout UI (so we don't hit global defaults)
2) Add a safety gate: if >60% short-prompt traffic, cap `max_delay_ms` to 30
3) Create docs/alert that warns when applying large `max_delay_ms` to models with short-token distributions.

maya (oncall): Logged follow-up tasks:
- SRE-3121: Add per-route gating + rollout validation
- SRE-3122: Alert rule for p99 > 3x baseline during config rollouts
- RUNTIME-762: Add early-flush optimization for small token counts

anika (support): I'll send a customer-facing note: apology, description of what happened, what we changed (override + rollback), and timeline.

maya (oncall): Marking this thread resolved for the immediate incident. Will keep alert retention for 24h and verify no regressions.

liam (runtime): Quick note — let's avoid blanket rollouts for batching config in the future. Use canary and per-model pilot. :+1:

maya (oncall): Agreed. Thanks team. Closing but leaving follow-ups in backlog. :white_check_mark:
